items.pronunciation_notes: A long uu and a retroflex ट with the tongue curled back: juutaa, two syllables.

learn.explanation_en: जूता is a shoe. It is masculine and ends in -ा, so both the gender and the plural are predictable, giving जूते. As with English, the plural is what you will normally hear, since shoes come in pairs and are talked about as a set.

examples.note: काला takes -ा because जूता is masculine.
The -ा becomes -े in the plural.
नया becomes नए for a masculine plural.

practice.question: जूता
practice.explanation_en: जूता is a shoe. चप्पल is an open sandal or slipper.

game.question_en: राम ___ जूता — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: जूता is masculine, so का. The -ा ending predicts correctly.

items.pronunciation_notes: The प्प stack holds the p with no breath released, and the final vowel drops: chappal.

learn.explanation_en: चप्पल is an open sandal or slipper, the footwear people slip off at the door. It is feminine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable — and worth noticing beside जूता, which is masculine. Two kinds of footwear, opposite genders. The word appeared in Module 3 as an example of the held प्प stack.

examples.note: नई is the feminine form of नया.
Feminine consonant endings take -एँ.
काला takes -ी because चप्पल is feminine.

common_error.why_en: चप्पल is feminine, so the colour takes -ी — while जूता, also footwear, takes -ा.

practice.question: चप्पल
practice.explanation_en: चप्पल is an open sandal or slipper. जूता is a closed shoe.

game.question_en: राम ___ चप्पल — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: चप्पल is feminine, so की. Its consonant ending predicts nothing.

items.pronunciation_notes: Retroflex ट with the tongue curled back, and a flat ओ with no glide: ṭopii.

learn.explanation_en: टोपी is a cap or hat of any kind. It ends in -ी and is feminine, so the ending predicts correctly, and the plural is टोपियाँ. You met the word in Module 2 as an example of the retroflex ट, so the tongue position should already be familiar.

examples.note: लाल never changes form.
The -ी becomes -ियाँ in the plural.
सफ़ेद also stays the same.

practice.question: टोपी
practice.explanation_en: टोपी is a cap or hat, worn on the head.

game.question_en: राम ___ टोपी — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: टोपी is feminine, so की. The -ी ending predicts correctly.

summary.recap_en: This level added जूता, चप्पल and टोपी. जूता and चप्पल are both footwear and take opposite genders, which is another reminder that meaning offers no shortcut either.

items.pronunciation_notes: The hook above त is र with no vowel, read before it: kurtaa rather than kutraa.

learn.explanation_en: कुर्ता is the long loose shirt worn across South Asia by men and women alike. It is masculine and ends in -ा, so the gender and plural are both predictable, giving कुर्ते. Like कुर्सी it contains the reph: र with no vowel written as a hook above the following letter but pronounced before it.

examples.note: सफ़ेद never changes form.
The -ा becomes -े in the plural.
नीला takes -ा because कुर्ता is masculine.

practice.question: कुर्ता
practice.explanation_en: कुर्ता is a long loose shirt. कमीज़ is the shorter fitted kind.

game.question_en: राम ___ कुर्ता — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: कुर्ता is masculine, so का. The -ा ending predicts correctly.

items.pronunciation_notes: The inherent vowel on ल drops, so the word is salvaar in two syllables.

learn.explanation_en: सलवार is the loose trousers gathered at the ankle, worn with a कमीज़ — together they make the सलवार-कमीज़. It is feminine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable. Conveniently both halves of the outfit are feminine, so any colour describing either takes the same form.

examples.note: नई is the feminine form of नया.
Feminine consonant endings take -एँ.
हरा takes -ी because सलवार is feminine.

practice.question: सलवार
practice.explanation_en: सलवार is the loose trousers worn with a कमीज़.

game.question_en: राम ___ सलवार — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: सलवार is feminine, so की. Its consonant ending gives no clue.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted ज़ is a z sound, and the ओ is flat with no glide: mozaa.

learn.explanation_en: मोज़ा is a sock. It is masculine and ends in -ा, so the gender and plural are predictable, giving मोज़े — and like shoes, socks are usually spoken of in the plural. The word carries the dotted ज़ from Module 2 and came into Hindi from Persian, as so much of the clothing vocabulary did.

examples.note: सफ़ेद never changes form.
The -ा becomes -े in the plural.
काला takes -ा in the singular.

practice.question: मोज़ा
practice.explanation_en: मोज़ा is a sock. जूता is the shoe that goes over it.

game.question_en: राम ___ मोज़ा — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: मोज़ा is masculine, so का. The -ा ending predicts correctly.

summary.recap_en: This level covered कुर्ता, सलवार and मोज़ा. Most of the clothing vocabulary arrived through Persian, which is why so many of these words carry a dotted letter.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the last clothing word, and then verbs — which behave differently again.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dot before ट is read as the retroflex nasal, and the ऐ is a single open vowel: paiṇṭ.

learn.explanation_en: पैंट is trousers, borrowed from English but treated as a singular noun: one pair is एक पैंट, not a plural as in English. It is feminine and ends in a consonant, so the gender is unpredictable. Note that it is feminine while its English-borrowed neighbour गिलास is masculine — borrowing settles nothing about gender.

examples.note: नीला takes -ी because पैंट is feminine.
The same feminine ending again.
Feminine consonant endings take -एँ.

common_error.why_en: पैंट is feminine, so an inflecting colour has to take its -ी form.

practice.question: पैंट
practice.explanation_en: पैंट is trousers, and Hindi treats one pair as singular.

game.question_en: राम ___ पैंट — का, के or की?
game.explanation_en: पैंट is feminine, so की — while गिलास, also borrowed from English, is masculine.

items.pronunciation_notes: A flat ओ with no glide, then a light ह: honaa, two syllables.

learn.explanation_en: होना means to be, and it is the most important verb in the language. Every Hindi verb is named by its infinitive, which always ends in -ना, and the part before that ending is the stem — here हो. The stem is what every other form is built from, so it is worth spotting from the start. Verbs are not nouns, so they carry no gender of their own.

examples.note: The infinitive after a describing word.
A very common pairing.
Literally 'to be big', used for growing up.

practice.question: होना
practice.explanation_en: होना is to be. करना is to do.

game.question_en: होना — which part is the stem, once -ना is removed?
game.explanation_en: Take -ना off the infinitive and हो is what remains. Every other form of this verb is built on that stem.

items.pronunciation_notes: The inherent vowel on र drops, so the word is karnaa in two syllables rather than three.

learn.explanation_en: करना means to do or to make, and it is the workhorse of the language: Hindi builds enormous numbers of expressions by pairing a noun or adjective with करना. Its stem is कर. The middle vowel drops in speech, so the word has two syllables and not three, which is the medial schwa behaviour from Module 3.

examples.note: Literally 'to make clean' — this pattern is everywhere.
Another adjective paired with करना.
The same pattern again, with a dotted letter.

practice.question: करना
practice.explanation_en: करना is to do or to make. होना is to be.

game.question_en: करना — which part is the stem, once -ना is removed?
game.explanation_en: Removing -ना from करना leaves कर, and every other form of the verb is built on it.

summary.recap_en: This level finished the clothing words with पैंट and introduced the first two verbs. Every Hindi verb is named by an infinitive ending in -ना, and the part before that ending is the stem that all other forms are built from.
summary.next_up_en: Next: जाना, आना and देखना — three more verbs and three more stems.

items.pronunciation_notes: Two long aa vowels and a dental न: jaanaa.

learn.explanation_en: जाना means to go, and its stem is जा. Along with आना it makes up the pair you will use most often in giving and following directions. Notice how short the stem is: with verbs ending in -ाना, removing the -ना leaves just one syllable, which is normal rather than a sign that something is missing.

examples.note: The place comes before the verb in Hindi.
बाज़ार carries the dotted ज़.
वापस never changes form.

practice.question: जाना
practice.explanation_en: जाना is to go. आना is to come.

game.question_en: जाना — which part is the stem, once -ना is removed?
game.explanation_en: Removing -ना leaves जा, a single syllable, which is the stem.

items.pronunciation_notes: Both vowels are long, and the word opens with the full letter आ: aanaa.

learn.explanation_en: आना means to come, and its stem is simply आ — the shortest stem in the language. It pairs with जाना everywhere, and the two together cover most of what you need for movement. Later on आना also carries the sense of knowing how to do something, but that construction belongs to a much later module.

examples.note: The same pattern as घर जाना.
वापस works with both verbs.
A fixed pair, used as a phrase.

practice.question: आना
practice.explanation_en: आना is to come. जाना is to go.

game.question_en: आना — which part is the stem, once -ना is removed?
game.explanation_en: Removing -ना leaves आ, a single vowel, and that is the whole stem.

items.pronunciation_notes: The inherent vowel on ख drops, so the word is dekhnaa in two syllables, and the ए is flat with no glide.

learn.explanation_en: देखना covers seeing, looking at and watching, so it does the work of several English verbs. Its stem is देख. The middle vowel drops in speech, giving two syllables rather than three, and the ख is aspirated, so a clear puff of air follows it.

examples.note: The thing seen comes before the verb.
The same word covers watching.
And seeing too — one verb for all three.

practice.question: देखना
practice.explanation_en: देखना is to see, to look at, or to watch — all three.

game.question_en: देखना — which part is the stem, once -ना is removed?
game.explanation_en: Removing -ना leaves देख, which is the stem every other form is built on.

summary.recap_en: This level added जाना, आना and देखना. Stripping -ना gives जा, आ and देख — stems of one syllable or even one vowel, which is normal rather than a sign that anything is missing.
summary.next_up_en: Next: पीना, बोलना and लिखना complete this run of verbs.

items.pronunciation_notes: Unaspirated प with no puff of air, then a long ii: piinaa.

learn.explanation_en: पीना means to drink, and its stem is पी. It also covers smoking — सिगरेट पीना is how you say to smoke a cigarette, which surprises English speakers but follows the same logic as taking something in. Keep the opening sound free of breath, since फीना with a puff is not a word.

examples.note: The drink comes before the verb.
You will hear this offered constantly.
The same pattern with a third drink.

practice.question: पीना
practice.explanation_en: पीना is to drink. खाना, which you met as a noun, is the verb to eat.

game.question_en: पीना — which part is the stem, once -ना is removed?
game.explanation_en: Removing -ना leaves पी, a single syllable, which is the stem.

items.pronunciation_notes: The inherent vowel on ल drops, giving bolnaa in two syllables, with a flat ओ and no glide.

learn.explanation_en: बोलना means to speak or to say, and its stem is बोल. Use it for speaking a language and for speaking in general. The middle vowel drops, so the word has two syllables. Much later, in the module on the ने construction, बोलना turns out to be one of a small group of verbs that behave unusually — but that is a long way off.

examples.note: The language comes before the verb.
A useful request when you are learning.
कम never changes form.

practice.question: बोलना
practice.explanation_en: बोलना is to speak or to say. सुनना is to hear.

game.question_en: बोलना — which part is the stem, once -ना is removed?
game.explanation_en: Removing -ना leaves बोल, which is the stem.

items.pronunciation_notes: The ि matra is drawn before ल but read after it, and the inherent vowel on ख drops: likhnaa.

learn.explanation_en: लिखना means to write, and its stem is लिख. You met the word back in Module 2 as an example of the aspirated ख, so the puff of air in the middle should be familiar. It pairs naturally with पढ़ना, to read, which contains the breathy flap and is the other half of literacy vocabulary.

examples.note: The thing written comes before the verb.
The same pattern with a longer object.
पत्र keeps its final vowel because it ends in a conjunct with र.

practice.question: लिखना
practice.explanation_en: लिखना is to write. पढ़ना is to read.

game.question_en: लिखना — which part is the stem, once -ना is removed?
game.explanation_en: Removing -ना leaves लिख, which is the stem every other form is built on.

summary.recap_en: This level completed eight verbs with पीना, बोलना and लिखना. Every one is named by an infinitive in -ना, and every one hides a stem underneath it — पी, बोल and लिख — which is what the next modules will build on.
summary.next_up_en: Next: more verbs, including the ones for eating, reading, taking and giving.
